answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring their identity in cryptographic attestation chains and verifying computation via zero-knowledge proofs. To deter swarms, joining requires a staking bond scaling superlinearly as O(N^2), causing exponential capital exhaustion. Unlike the fable where a tiny sparrow flaunts a borrowed peacock plume, an imposter swarm faces prohibitive costs that mathematically enforce identity integrity across the network.
